#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored
  add FILE --section TITLE   FILE holds one row line, its # cell `?` (or the
                             seven cells after it); numbers it max + 1 and
                             inserts it in that section's table in number
                             order
  note N TEXT                appends TEXT to row N's notes
  close N --commit HASH --test NAME [--note TEXT] [--claim C] [--class C]
        [--spec C] [--found-by C]
                             after the fix has landed: HASH must be in HEAD's
                             history and NAME a test under the test folders;
                             writes the one-line FIXED row (the claim's first
                             sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed
                             HASH; full text: history, row N`); the options
                             give cells the old row lacks in the template's form
  duplicate N --of M [--add TEXT] [--claim C] [--class C] [--spec C]
        [--reproducer C] [--found-by C]
                             makes row N a DUPLICATE pointer to row M (notes
                             `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`);
                             --add appends TEXT to row M's notes
  check [--rows FILE] [--base COMMIT] [--summary]
                             lints every row against the template, and the
                             tables' headers, numbers and order; --rows lints
                             a file holding only row lines instead; --base
                             also checks that every row at COMMIT is the same
                             line now or has its full earlier line in the
                             history file, and that the set of row numbers is
                             unchanged; --summary prints only the counts by
                             rule; exit 1 on any failure

Text given on the command line (TEXT, C) has its bare pipes escaped.
"""

import argparse
import collections
import fcntl
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unicodedata

TOOLS = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))
TREE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(TOOLS)))   # the checkout this tool is in

LEDGER_REL = 'explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md'
HISTORY_NAME = 'fortress-gap-ledger-history.md'
LOCK_NAME = '.ledger.lock'

HEADER = ('#', 'claim', 'status', 'class', 'spec citation', 'reproducer', 'found by', 'notes / workaround')
CELLS = ('num', 'claim', 'status', 'class', 'spec', 'reproducer', 'found_by', 'notes')
# A header title to its cell; row 83's table names its notes "why unsettled".
HEADER_NAMES = dict(zip(HEADER, CELLS), **{'why unsettled': 'notes'})

STATUSES = ('POSITIVE-VERIFIED', 'NEGATIVE-VERIFIED', 'NEGATIVE-BOUNDED', 'CONTESTED', 'RETIRED', 'FIXED', 'DUPLICATE')
CLOSED = ('FIXED', 'DUPLICATE', 'RETIRED')
NO_CLASS = ('POSITIVE-VERIFIED', 'RETIRED')
KINDS = ('implementation gap', 'library gap vs spec', 'library bug', 'design limit', 'deliberate', 'typesetter', 'packaging')
AREAS = ('parser', 'walk', 'checker', 'codegen', 'runtime', 'library', 'prelude', 'specification', 'tests', 'tools')
DASH = '—'
LIMITS = (('row', 1200), ('claim', 300), ('reproducer', 200), ('found_by', 60), ('notes', 700))
HEAD_CLAIM = 150      # of a row's claim that heads and find print
SHORT_NOTES = 300     # of a row's notes that show --short prints
FIND_ROWS = 10        # rows find prints without --all
VACANT = {148}        # never used: run-c's row 148 was merged into row 8
FROZEN = 'Specification-1.0-frozen/'
PLACEHOLDERS = ('?', '#', 'N', '')
TEST_FOLDERS_EXTRA = ('shelltests', 'compiler_regressions', 'long_term_not_working', 'not_passing_yet', 'test_library')

SEP = re.compile(r'\|\s*:?-{3,}')
ROW = re.compile(r'\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|')
STRICT = re.compile(r'(?<!\\)\|')
LENIENT = re.compile(r'(?<!\\)\|(?=\s|$)')
CLASS = re.compile(r'(%s) \((%s)\)$' % ('|'.join(map(re.escape, KINDS)), '|'.join(AREAS)))
SPEC_FILE = re.compile(r'((?:[\w.+-]+/)*[\w.+-]+\.tex)(:\d[\d,:\s-]*)?')
QUOTED = re.compile(r'"([^"]+)"|“([^”]+)”')
TEX_HEAD = re.compile(r'\s*\\(?:part|chapter|section|subsection|subsubsection|paragraph)\*?\s*(?:\[[^\]]*\])?\s*\{(.*)\}')
PATH_EXT = re.compile(r'\.(fss|fsi|java|scala|tex|tick|rats|test|md|js|py|sh|out|txt|ast|xml|jj|log|csv|json|html|properties)$')
HASH = re.compile(r'\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b')


class LedgerError(Exception):
    pass

FACTS.md:63
- F-70 **No static parameter of the one library is bounded by `Object`; the compiled checker checks a static argument written at a dotted method call against its bound, but not one written at a top-level function call; and walk stops on a tuple, `()` or an arrow for a written `Object`.** The library's result-only parameters are unbounded, as P-48 decides (F-84), and six, `cast` among them, write `extends Any`. The specification's examples and the compiler tests write `extends Object`. At a dotted call the checker puts the written arguments into each bound and refuses one that misses it, "No such method" (row 651, fixed); at a top-level call it matches kinds only (row 470). Walk's stop is an `InterpreterBug`, not a type error (row 471). Gated by `compiler_tests/MethodStaticArgsBoundNamesOther*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-result-bounds/REPORT.md` section 10; `compile-ladder/rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 1.

FACTS.md:77
- F-84 **The one library's numbers, orderings, `List` and natives answer their declared types, and its result-only parameters are unbounded, as the team declared them.** `fail`, `builtinPrimitive` and `List`'s nullary comprehension carry an unbounded `T` (P-48), so where `()` is expected their instance is `()`. `MatchFailure` is unchecked. Left: `LexicographicOrder` (row 634's list half) and `QQ`'s power (rows 438, 445). Gated by `tests/NumberOrderListDeclarations.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-number-order-slips/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 5.

FACTS.md:208
- F-181 **The code generator refuses every function, object and trait declaration that carries a `where` clause or a contract (row 701).** The `fortress-repo` skill's `references/compiler.md`, "What the compiled path cannot compile yet", gives this refusal and the constructs that the code generator has no case for, a local function among them (row 304). An array comprehension has no case either. Past the guard, `NatParam`'s clause of bindings only compiles and runs, and opening its value at a call fails verification (row 307). Detail: `coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md` section 3; `perf-probes/where-clauses/REPORT.md` A.7.

POSITIONS.md:47
- P-48 **A type parameter that a call's arguments do not fix takes its bound, never `Bottom`.** Its instance is the intersection of its upper bounds, constrained by the call's static return type, never the arguments' union or the value's type alone. The rule is the team's later word (POPL 2019). He ranks the team's later work above his own reading. It sets the instance, not which declaration runs (P-46). MicroGPT's types are concrete, so it is untouched. The library keeps the team's unbounded declarations. Built under walk for a reduction or comprehension that writes no static argument by climb batch 15 (`20474c144`). Still to build: a compiled dispatcher that carries the static return type (row 538, PLAN phase 5).

POSITIONS.md:66
- P-152 **Exclusion between two generic declarations is read over the whole parameter type, on both paths (the specification's existential reduction).** Two declarations whose parameter types exclude each other only together, through a shared parameter that fixes one static argument, are read as the specification reads them: the pair is valid where the declared domains meet the overloading rules. Walk and the compiled checker both change to read the whole parameter type, so that rows 740 and 741 close, and walk loads the program that it refused after climb batch 16. Why: the specification states this reading, and the paths should match the designers' text. Still to build: a probe to find the algorithm on both paths, then a batch rung on each.

- P-45 **Overloads may differ in their static parameters (answer 9).** The specification drops its sentence that forbids it and states the type group's 2011 model, which the checker runs; the old sentence stays as superseded text. The checker keeps the paper's three overloading rules, checks the Return Type Rule over every instance, and requires two generic declarations in the more-specific relation to agree on their static parameters position by position, as Java's overriding rule does (row 398). Walk dispatches on declared domains, not by the order of the declarations, and its load check reads every pair of generic declarations on their declared domains by the checker's rules, with no parameter pair required to exclude, so that walk and the checker accept the same pairs (row 159). The library repairs its refused families with its own exclusions, and no model line changes. The judgement's smaller choices took the record's defaults, listed for his review in `PLAN.md`. Built: walk's load check over every pair of functions with static parameters, by climb batch 17's rung G. Not built: a functional method of a generic trait or object is still compared on its instances (F-26), the Meet Rule's search matches only some domains (row 539), and rows 740 and 741 wait on P-152. The one pair on which rung G's reading makes walk and the checker disagree is row 759's: walk refuses `g[\T\](a: T)` beside `g(a: Any)`, and the checker accepts it.

POSITIONS.md:45
- P-46 **A conversion makes a call possible, and never changes which declaration runs when one already fits.** Declarations are chosen on declared domains, by applicability and then specificity (P-45). The chosen one is instantiated by answer 8's promotion (P-74), its coercions inserted statically. So beside a plain arm over `Any`, a generic arm over `T extends Number` runs at `ZZ64` for a mixed-width call. A numeral whose candidate types are incomparable reads as `ZZ32`, or as `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by its magnitude. Why: generic code is never fast, and he wants code that a JVM can specialise. His own broader rule, to convert toward a specific declaration before a generic one, is not taken. Both paths infer static arguments with coercion and the same promotion, and P-49 orders the checker's attempts. Still open: the dispatch between two generic declarations (row 537, PLAN phase 5).

- P-74 **Mixed integer widths convert by declared coercions (answer 8, to PLAN item 8): each wider type declares a `coerce` from each narrower one, as the compiler prelude does.** An exact conversion is implicit and a lossy one explicit: `ZZ32` and integer numerals coerce into `RR64`, and `ZZ64` into `RR64` stays explicit (P-66).
